requirement:
HC represents a FIXME acknowledgment as a graph node and exposes its tracking
issue relationships as labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes. A named FIXME also
connects the acknowledgment to the requirement whose gap it acknowledges;
an unnamed FIXME connects directly to its tracking issues.
Each issue named by the acknowledgment is available through its tracking edges.
rationale:
`requirements.sdk.habeas.fixme_graph` has no {test} or :test: references. A text search for `fixme_graph` finds only the requirement declaration and a {fixme} reference. A search of `src` for FIXME and tracking-edge code finds only FIXME parsing, summary and judgment tests in `src/fixme.rs`, `src/authoring/mod.rs` and similar files. None of them build a graph node for an acknowledgment or expose its tracking edges.

The requirement sets these obligations, and none has a test:
- A FIXME acknowledgment is represented as a graph node.
- Its tracking issues are exposed as labeled edges to GitHub issue nodes.
- A named FIXME also connects to the requirement whose gap it acknowledges.
- An unnamed FIXME connects directly to its tracking issues.
- Every issue the acknowledgment names is available through its tracking edges.

The code carrying these out has conditionals, such as the named versus unnamed split and the choice of edge targets. So the untested-obligation exemption doesn't apply.

The gap is acknowledged. `src/sdk.rs#enum[HabeasNode]` carries a {fixme} reference to this requirement. Its body says graph nodes and tracking-issue edges are deferred, and that named and unnamed acknowledgments, source ownership and multiple issue targets have no tests. That matches the missing-test gap. The issue it names, nikomatsakis/habeas-codicem#26, is open.
